appearance.organs.panicle.note: The panicle's layout, the model's choice after FNA's accounts of the genus and species (volume 24), as search results quote them (the pages were not read): a panicle 4 to 20 cm, typically pyramidal, the lower branches spreading and the upper appressed; its primary branches one-sided and naked below, with dense clusters of nearly sessile spikelets toward their tips. Drawn as 8 branches, each a dense spike of about 24 spikelets on its upper half, the upper branches shorter with fewer. The spikelet's florets, glumes, lemmas and awns come from the traits by the Poales rules; colours by eye, green with purplish glumes.

traits.upper_glume_length_m.note: FNA's account of the species (Allred, volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): glumes 3 to 5 mm, shorter than the florets; lemmas 4 to 8 mm.

traits.lemma_length_m.note: FNA's account of the species (Allred, volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): lemmas 4 to 8 mm, scabridulous; the spikelets 5 to 8 mm, nearly sessile.

traits.awn_insertion.note: FNA's account of the genus (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): the lemmas taper to a short awn, so it leaves the lemma's tip.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a coarse, introduced bunchgrass with broad, folded, blue-green blades and one-sided panicles of dense, clustered spikelets. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: blue-green blades; green to straw panicles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: GrassBase's account of the species: a tufted perennial, its culms 15 to 140 cm long; blades 10 to 45 cm by 2 to 14 mm; a dense, one-sided panicle 2 to 30 cm long; spikelets 5 to 9 mm, of 2 to 5 fertile florets above two unlike glumes; the lemma's awn 0.5 to 1.5 mm.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hitchcock (p. 184): culms in large tussocks; no rhizomes named (Abrams 1923, Dactylis no. 1: plants in large tussocks).

traits.clonal.note: Hitchcock (p. 184): a tussock grass, its culms in large tussocks with no rhizomes or stolons named, so it does not spread beyond its tuft.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 1 (Dactylis glomerata, fig. 449): flowers June-August as an escape along roadsides and waste places in the Pacific States.
